prompt: Company profile: Precision machine shop in Erie, Pennsylvania; 30 employees; a very small quantity generator (VSQG) normally generating about 40 kg/month of hazardous waste. Situation: The shop plans a one-time decommissioning and cleanout of an old vapor degreaser containing trichloroethylene (TCE); the cleanout will generate roughly 1,600 kg of TCE still bottoms and spent solvent in a single month, then generation returns to normal. Pennsylvania DEP administers an authorized RCRA program. Ask: Identify the compliance obligations this situation creates or affects for the compliance-obligations register. For each obligation: state the requirement, its source, its applicability to this company, the ISO clause it maps to (ISO 14001 6.1.3 / ISO 45001 6.1.3), and how and when compliance should be evaluated (9.1.2).
response:
**Compliance Obligations Register – One‑Time Vapor Degreaser Cleanout**  
*Precision Machine Shop – Erie, PA – 30 employees – VSQG (normally ≤ 40 kg/month hazardous waste)*  

**Event:** Decommissioning and cleanout of a vapor degreaser containing trichloroethylene (TCE) will generate ≈ 1 600 kg of spent solvent and still bottoms in a single calendar month. After the cleanout, generation returns to normal VSQG levels.

**Regulatory Trigger:** Under RCRA, generator status is determined monthly. The 1 600 kg quantity exceeds the Large Quantity Generator (LQG) threshold (≥ 1 000 kg/month). Therefore, for that month the facility is an LQG and must meet all LQG requirements (unless the state‑adopted “episodic generation” rule is used). Pennsylvania DEP administers an authorized RCRA program; as of 2023 the EPA’s 2016 Generator Improvements Rule (including episodic generation) has **not** been adopted in Pennsylvania, so full LQG compliance is required.
